subject: Clarify: 'We do not train on customer data' — erase procedure and retention carveouts
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintechco.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question re: statement 'we do not train on customer data' — retention edge cases

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the platform overview yesterday. Our legal and security teams are reviewing the vendor statements and want a few clarifications around the phrase you use in the public docs: "We do not train on customer data". Specifically, they asked:

- Do backups, debug snapshots, or KV cache contents ever get used to update models or training corpora?
- What are the retention windows for live request logs vs ephemeral KV caches vs nightly backups?
- Are there any circumstances (legal hold, fraud investigation) where customer content is kept beyond the stated window?
- Do you provide an attestation or SOC2 annex that explicitly says customer text is excluded from model training?

Could you point us to a one-page summary we can share with legal, and confirm whether you can sign a clause in our contract that forbids derivative model training on our content?

Appreciate a short write-up today if possible — we have an internal review on Monday.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Security, FinTechCo
security-contact@fintechco.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Question re: statement 'we do not train on customer data' — retention edge cases

Folks,

Forwarding FinTechCo's questions — they need a concise, authoritative answer for legal. Key asks: backups/snapshots/KV cache usage, retention windows, legal hold behavior, and an attestation.

My draft responses below (first pass). Can you confirm and add anything I missed? I attached the current erase playbook and the dataflow diagram to share after we align.

DRAFT points to confirm:
- Redwood does not use customer-provided content (text, files, request payloads) to train or fine-tune production models.
- Telemetry and aggregated metrics (e.g., token counts, latency histograms) may be used to improve service quality; these are not customer-text and are pseudonymized/aggregated.
- KV caches are ephemeral and exist only for low-latency inference; default retention is 14 days and they are not surfaced to training pipelines.
- Debug snapshots (taken on failure) are retained 14 days by default; customers may request earlier purge or opt-in extended retention for troubleshooting.
- Nightly backups/snapshots are retained for 90 days to support restore; backups are excluded from model training and are retained only for ops recovery.
- Legal hold requests can extend retention until release; we record holds and can provide evidence of the hold and subsequent deletion.
- We can provide an attestation letter (SOC2 addendum-style) stating we do not leverage customer content for model training; legal to sign contract language is possible but needs Escalation if they request indefinite guarantees.

Please review and mark changes inline.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Question re: statement 'we do not train on customer data' — retention edge cases

Jonas — thanks for the draft. A few clarifications from Product/Privacy that I think are important to call out explicitly (I'll add to the playbook):

1) Definition: when we say "we do not train on customer data" we mean we do not ingest raw customer text or files into any model training/fine-tuning corpus or update weights of any production models using identifiable customer content. We do occasionally use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for internal model-quality signals (e.g., distribution drift), and we never surface customer text on those signals.

2) KV cache and inference caches: these are implementation-level caches for latency. Default retention is 14 days; for Dedicated/Private customers we can configure shorter windows (even session-only) via config. KV caches are never copied to offline training stores.

3) Debug snapshots & ephemeral logs: debug snapshots capture request+context+stack traces for failed requests. Default retention 14 days; they are stored in encrypted buckets and are accessible only to SRE/Support under strict RBAC. They are not part of the training dataset.

4) Backups & archives: backup retention for hosted accounts is 90 days; backups are for disaster recovery only and are excluded from model training. Long-term archival (beyond 90 days) requires explicit contractual terms and separate approvals.

5) Legal hold: legal hold will pause deletion and extend retention until lifted. We log holds in an audit record and can provide timestamped attestation of hold and subsequent purge. Holds are rare but necessary for investigations; they are scoped and timeboxed where possible.

6) Exceptions & derivatives: we do not train derivative models on customer content without opt-in. There is a small internal exception for synthetic data used to improve tooling (anonymized and vetted) — any such program requires legal approval and customer opt-in.

7) Evidence & attestation: we can produce a signed attestation and SOC2 annex confirming exclusion from training. For customers wanting contractual language, propose a standard "No-Derivative-Training" clause with defined carveouts (telemetry, legal hold) — Legal can review.

I'll update the playbook and create a 1-page summary for FinTechCo. Suggest offering a 30-minute call to walk through the diagram and the attestation.

- Priyom
Product Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintechco.com>, security-contact@fintechco.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Question re: statement 'we do not train on customer data' — retention edge cases

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed questions and for the patience while we pulled this together. Below is a concise summary you can share with your legal team; attached are the redwood-erase-playbook-v1.2.docx and dataflow-and-backups.pdf for more technical detail. If you'd like, we can also provide a signed attestation letter and the SOC2 annex which explicitly confirms exclusion from model training.

Executive summary (short):
- Redwood does not use raw customer content (requests, files, chat transcripts) to train or fine-tune production models.
- Aggregated, de-identified telemetry metrics may be used for product and quality improvements; these do not contain customer text.
- Ephemeral caches (KV caches, inference caches) default retention: 14 days; not used for training. Configurable shorter retention for Dedicated/Private.
- Debug snapshots (on-demand for failures): default retention 14 days; accessible under RBAC; not used for training.
- Nightly backups: retained 90 days for recovery; excluded from training. Long-term archival beyond 90 days is by contract only.
- Legal hold will suspend deletion; we log and can provide time-stamped evidence of holds and subsequent deletion when lifted.

Contractual/attestation options:
- We can provide a signed attestation (No-Derivative-Training) and include a SOC2 annex confirming our controls.
- If you need specific contract language, we propose the standard clause we use (attached). If FinTechCo requires stricter guarantees (e.g., zero-exceptions for legal hold), we will need an escalation to Legal/Commercial; those requests are handled as carve-outs.

Next steps:
1) I attached the playbook and dataflow diagram for your team.
2) Let us know if you want the signed attestation; I'll route to Legal.
3) Happy to meet — propose Mon 10:00am PT for a 30-min call to walk through the details.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
